latest_release.name: 2026.10.2 : Bug Fix Release
latest_release.body: ## What's Fixed - **Fields and formulas** - Changing a field type on PostgreSQL keeps every value that fits, renaming a field updates the formulas that use it, and a math error blanks only its own row. - **Filters** - *Is any of* matches the exact select option, empty filter groups are removed, and date filters work on lookups of date formulas and rollups. - **More filters** - Date filters with a wrong value are rejected on save, and filters on cross-base links apply for people who can see the linked table. - **Grid and records** - Escape cancels a cell edit, pasting a value that does not fit keeps the old one, and one edit makes one revision entry. - **Expanded records** - Ctrl/Cmd+F uses the browser's find while a record is expanded, and *Create & Link* from a new record creates the linked record when you save. - **Typing** - The first key typed with a Chinese or Japanese IME reaches the cell, and a barcode scanner in the link picker links the scanned record. - **Dates and numbers** - Dates before year 100 keep their year, Decimal fields from external databases use the column's scale, and Calendar weekdays follow the UI language. - **Rich text** - Rich text and code blocks keep their content and indentation after save and reload. [Learn more](/docs/product/tables/fields/field-types/text-based/rich-text) - **Comments** - Text in angle brackets, such as `Name `, is kept in comments. - **Links** - *Create & Link* on a self-link links the right way, and deleting a table from Trash removes its link fields. - **Lookups** - A Lookup through a many-to-many link keeps the display value of the linked records, and filters on nested Lookups apply the Lookup's own conditions. [Learn more](/docs/product/tables/fields/field-types/links-based/lookup#applying-filters) - **External databases** - PostgreSQL generated columns are read-only, MySQL DateTime rollups show the right time, and links to a table with a composite primary key are rejected before anything is created. - **Trash** - Deleting or restoring a record keeps its linked records that are already in Trash listed there. [Learn more](/docs/product/projects/project-trash#restoring-an-entry) - **Duplicate** - Duplicating a project or table skips filters on cross-base links it does not copy, and works with column defaults that contain `?`. [Learn more](/docs/product/projects/actions-on-project#duplicate-project) - **Imports and exports** - Excel imports keep sheet names, and exports write link display values. - **CSV import** - Merging a CSV on Id updates existing records, and webhooks and workflows of imported records see their links. - **Kanban** - Boards with more than 25 stacks show every stack after *Collapse all*. [Learn more](/docs/product/tables/views/view-types/kanban#collapse-stack) - **Calendar** - A calendar on a date rollup shows records as all-day events. - **Classic apps** - A dashboard group filter applies to every widget, form pages send *Email responses*, people pickers list only people who have access, and table pages show number separators. - **Forms** - Forms that require sign-in open after sign-in, with no redirect loop. - **Workflows** - Send email accepts a comma-separated list, run history shows why a run failed before its first step, scripts run with the NocoAI integration, and a workflow that can never run is not left Live. [Learn more](/docs/workflows/nodes/action-nodes/send-email) - **Webhooks** - The sample payload shows link fields as real payloads do. [Learn more](/docs/product/tables/table-operations/webhook/create-webhook#configuring-webhook) - **Table Sync** - Paste-link syncs from a password-protected shared view accept the password. [Learn more](/docs/product/sync/nocodb-sync#source) - **Security** - Shared views and shared dashboards return only the fields th

# Join Our Community [![Stargazers repo roster for @nocodb/nocodb](http://reporoster.com/stars/nocodb/nocodb)](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/stargazers) # Installation ## Docker with SQLite ```bash docker run -d \ --name noco \ -v "$(pwd)"/nocodb:/usr/app/data/ \ -p 8080:8080 \ nocodb/nocodb:latest ``` ## Docker with PG ```bash docker run -d \ --name noco \ -v "$(pwd)"/nocodb:/usr/app/data/ \ -p 8080:8080 \ -e NC_DB="pg://host.docker.internal:5432?u=root&p=password&d=d1" \ -e NC_AUTH_JWT_SECRET="569a1821-0a93-45e8-87ab-eb857f20a010" \ nocodb/nocodb:latest ``` ## Auto-upstall Auto-upstall is a single command that sets up NocoDB on a server for production usage. Behind the scenes it auto-generates docker-compose for you. ```bash bash <(curl -sSL http://install.nocodb.com/noco.sh) <(mktemp) ``` Auto-upstall does the following: 🕊 - 🐳 Automatically installs all pre-requisites like docker, docker-compose - 🚀 Automatically installs NocoDB with PostgreSQL, Redis, Traefik gateway using Docker Compose. 🐘 🗄️ 🌐 - 🔄 Automatically upgrades NocoDB to the latest version when you run the command again. - 🔒 Automatically setups SSL and also renews it. Needs a domain or subdomain as input while installation. > install.nocodb.com/noco.sh script can be found [here in our github](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nocodb/nocodb/develop/docker-compose/1_Auto_Upstall/noco.sh) ## Other Methods > Prebuilt binaries are no longer published. The `get.nocodb.com` download links have been discontinued; please use one of the Docker based methods above instead. For more installation methods such as Docker Compose, Kubernetes and Helm, please refer to [our docs](https://nocodb.com/docs/self-hosting) > When running locally access nocodb by visiting: [http://localhost:8080/dashboard](http://localhost:8080/dashboard) # Screenshots ![2](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/assets/86527202/a127c05e-2121-4af2-a342-128e0e2d0291) ![3](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/assets/86527202/674da952-8a06-4848-a0e8-a7b02d5f5c88) ![4](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/assets/86527202/cbc5152a-9caf-4f77-a8f7-92a9d06d025b) ![5](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/assets/86527202/dc75dfdc-c486-4f5a-a853-2a8f9e6b569a) ![5](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35857179/194844886-a17006e0-979d-493f-83c4-0e72f5a9b716.png) ![7](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/assets/86527202/be64e619-7295-43e2-aa95-cace4462b17f) ![8](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/assets/86527202/4538bf5a-371f-4ec1-a867-8197e5824286) ![8](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35857179/194844893-82d5e21b-ae61-41bd-9990-31ad659bf490.png) ![9](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35857179/194844897-cfd79946-e413-4c97-b16d-eb4d7678bb79.png) ![10](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35857179/194844902-c0122570-0dd5-41cf-a26f-6f8d71fefc99.png) ![11](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35857179/194844903-c1e47f40-e782-4f5d-8dce-6449cc70b181.png) ![12](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35857179/194844907-09277d3e-cbbf-465c-9165-6afc4161e279.png) # Features ### Rich Spreadsheet Interface - ⚡  Basic Operations: Create, Read, Update and Delete Tables, Columns, and Rows - ⚡  Fields Operations: Sort, Filter, Group, Hide / Unhide Columns - ⚡  Multiple Views Types: Grid (By default), Gallery, Form, Kanban and Calendar View - ⚡  View Permissions Types: Collaborative Views, & Locked Views - ⚡  Share Bases / Views: either Public or Private (with Password Protected) - ⚡  Variant Cell Types: ID, Links, Lookup, Rollup, SingleLineText, Attachment, Currency, Formula, User, etc - ⚡  Access Control with Roles: Fine-grained Access Control at different levels - ⚡  and more ... ### App Store for Workflow Automations We provide different integrations in three main categories. See App Store for details. - ⚡  Chat: Slack, Discord, Mattermost, and etc - ⚡  Email: AWS SES, SMTP, MailerSend, and etc - ⚡  Storage: AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Minio, and etc ### Programmatic Access We provide the following ways to let users programmatically invoke actions. You can use a token (either JWT or Social Auth) to sign your requests for authorization to NocoDB. - ⚡  REST APIs - ⚡  NocoDB SDK # Contributing Please refer to [Contribution Guide](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). # Why are we building this? Most internet businesses equip themselves with either spreadsheet or a database to solve their business needs. Spreadsheets are used by Billion+ humans collaboratively every single day. However, we are way off working at similar speeds on databases which are way more powerful tools when it comes to computing. Attempts to solve this with SaaS offerings have meant horrible access controls, vendor lock-in, data lock-in, abrupt price changes & most importantly a glass ceiling on what's possible in the future. # Our Mission Our mission is to provide the most powerful no-code interface for databases, accessible to every internet business across the world. By making this capability broadly available under a fair and sustainable model, we aim to democratise access to powerful computing tools and enable a billion-plus people to develop radical tinkering and building abilities on the internet. # License
